title: Crusader armies reach Antioch
summary: The crusaders reached Antioch and blockaded several gates. The city's mountain defences prevented a complete encirclement.
evidenceNote: The Gesta dates arrival to 20 October; Raymond's account places the siege's beginning around 21 October.

title: Winter shortages strain the siege
summary: Food shortages drove foraging expeditions and desertions while the siege continued.
evidenceNote: A sustained crisis, not a single dated incident. The date bounds organize the timeline.

title: A relief army is defeated near the lake
summary: Crusader cavalry defeated a relief force outside Antioch. Meanwhile, the soldiers left at the siege fought the city's garrison. Captured horses and supplies replenished the crusader army.
evidenceNote: This follows the date in Dickinson's annotated Gesta. The point marks the broader countryside, not a surveyed battlefield.

title: Workers are sought at St Symeon
summary: Bohemond and Raymond went to the port of St Symeon to bring workers for a fort facing Antioch's Bridge Gate. An English fleet had arrived on 4 March; the garrison attacked the besiegers left behind.
evidenceNote: The voyage's arrival has a specific date; the trip for workers is presented as an early-March episode. Map endpoints do not establish an exact route.

title: Antioch falls; the citadel holds out
summary: Firuz helped Bohemond's men enter Antioch. Killings followed the capture; the citadel remained in defenders' hands.
evidenceNote: The marker represents the city, not the entry tower.

title: Kerbogha besieges the conquerors
summary: Kerbogha's army arrived, trapping the crusaders inside Antioch. The besiegers had become the besieged.
evidenceNote: Arrival and encirclement unfolded over several days.

title: The claimed Holy Lance is found
summary: Peter Bartholomew's reported discovery encouraged believers, while Bishop Adhemar doubted his claims.
evidenceNote: A reported relic discovery; its sacred authenticity is not established.

title: The crusaders defeat Kerbogha
summary: The crusaders marched out to battle and defeated Kerbogha's army, ending the counter-siege.
evidenceNote: The marker is a schematic anchor outside the city, not a precise battlefield boundary.

title: The citadel surrenders
summary: After Kerbogha's defeat, the citadel's commander negotiated surrender to Bohemond.
evidenceNote: City-level placement; the citadel's footprint is not reconstructed here.
